answer.answer: Paragraph 14 most naturally makes confirmation independent of a request and demonstration conditional on an SFC request. Both concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; “to the SFC’s satisfaction” most directly qualifies demonstration. Footnote 5 specifies minimum content for confirmation and demonstration, but its unqualified wording supports a rival standing-demonstration reading. Without a request, confirmation remains expected; demonstration is untriggered under the main-text and integrated readings, but remains expected under the standing-footnote reading. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on an applicable SFC request. None of these trigger conclusions establishes fulfillment.

claims.proposition: Paragraph 14 distinguishes confirmation from request-triggered demonstration of the same stated subjects.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

claims.inference: Text and grammatical deduction: the inserted request condition most naturally qualifies “demonstrate”, leaving “confirm” unconditioned. The shared objects follow both verbs; the satisfaction standard most directly attaches to demonstration.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained circular to the entity, product, activity and assessment period.
Any applicable authorisation conditions, amendments, relaxations or additional guidance.
The required timing, form and evidential standard of confirmation.

claims.proposition: Footnote 5 adds minimum substantive content and a smart-contract assurance standard, while leaving a supported trigger dispute.
claims.status: Express content supported; trigger attachment disputed

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

claims.inference: Text: footnote 5 names both confirmation and demonstration and supplies minimum content. Its high-confidence wording concerns the absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws; the passage supplies no numerical confidence threshold or prescribed proof method. Interpretation is needed to reconcile its omission of a request condition with paragraph 14.
missing_premises: An authoritative resolution of how footnote 5 inherits or supplements the main-text request condition.
An applicable interpretation of “high level of confidence” and evidence sufficient to meet it.
Evidence of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and assessment of the relevant deployed smart contracts.

claims.proposition: No-request consequences depend on the demonstration reading and do not establish fulfillment.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction
Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

claims.inference: Conditional deduction: assuming no applicable request has actually been made, readings A and C do not activate demonstration, while reading B retains a standing expectation. Confirmation remains under all three. Absence of a request neither proves substantive compliance nor removes the underlying responsibilities.
missing_premises: Reliable facts establishing whether an applicable SFC request exists and its scope.
Resolution of the rival demonstration readings.
Actual compliance and assurance evidence; absence of a request is not such evidence.

claims.proposition: Paragraphs 15 and 16 impose distinct request-conditioned obtaining requirements, rather than equating demonstration with an audit or legal opinion.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.
Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

claims.inference: Text and deduction: each paragraph conditions its own obtaining requirement on an SFC request. Paragraph 15 concerns third-party audit or verification of the listed operational, ownership-record and smart-contract subjects. Paragraph 16 concerns a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. A paragraph 14 demonstration request does not automatically establish that either additional item was requested; its actual terms could cover multiple requirements.
missing_premises: The content and scope of each applicable request.
Whether the requested audit, verification or opinion was obtained and meets the applicable substantive requirements.
Any independent requirements to obtain these materials from other applicable provisions.

rival_readings: A — Main-text reading: demonstration requires an SFC request, concerns paragraph 14’s stated subjects and must satisfy the SFC. Footnote 5’s precise integration remains unresolved; this reading does not justify disregarding it.

B — Standing-footnote reading: footnote 5’s unqualified “confirm and demonstrate” supports demonstration without a request of its minimum content, including high-confidence smart-contract assurance. This reading faces the express main-text request condition and requires explaining how the two provisions coexist.

C — Integrated reading: footnote 5 specifies minimum content for both confirmation and demonstration, while demonstration inherits paragraph 14’s request trigger and SFC-satisfaction standard. This is the more coherent reading of the provisions together, as an interpretive judgment rather than established legal correctness.
unresolved: Whether the SFC-satisfaction wording also governs confirmation through the coordinated sentence; its clearest grammatical attachment is to demonstration.
The relationship between the SFC-satisfaction standard and high-confidence smart-contract assurance, including acceptable evidence and assessment methods.
Actual applicability, request facts and fulfillment remain unproved. A formal rule or solver accepting a reading would not resolve these legal and factual gaps.
